title: Fine-grained randomized simulation of unique-witness computation by hitting-set reconstruction

standard_prerequisites.name: Imported short-output black-box hitting-set generator and reconstruction [10, Theorem4.3], DPG reconstruction [11], standard quasilinear classes and error amplification
standard_prerequisites.source_reference: Exact imported hitting-set statement70 retained. Complete source-local approximation, weak symmetry, depth, Claim71, deterministic-avoider construction and witness reconstruction proof retained. Author fine-grained adaptations47/49/50 explicitly reference full earlier proofs, all of which are included here.

core_obligations: Prove fine-grained probabilistic-complexity promise approximation under NQL average-case easiness.
Bound probabilistic complexity of short hitting-set outputs using uniqueness of the long witness.
Turn the probabilistic approximation distinguisher into a deterministic function avoiding the hitting set by amplification and a union bound over promised inputs.
Use black-box reconstruction plus the fine-grained computational-depth bound to describe the long unique witness briefly and run the resulting one-sided simulation.
difficulty_reason: Independent non-routine hitting-set/avoider reconstruction handles unique witnesses of subexponential length: short hitting-set outputs are compressed, a randomized distinguisher is amplified and fixed into an avoider, and a black-box reconstruction recovers the long witness. This mechanism is additional to the direct polynomial-time UP witness compression of066.
